name: Caretaker's Talent
oracle_text:
(Gain the next level as a sorcery to add its ability.)
Whenever one or more tokens you control enter, draw a card. This ability triggers only once each turn.
{W}: Level 2
When this Class becomes level 2, create a token that's a copy of target token you control.
{3}{W}: Level 3
Creature tokens you control get +2/+2.
blocked_sentences: (Gain the next level as a sorcery to add its ability.)
When this Class becomes level 2, create a token that's a copy of target token you control.

needs.what: Class levels: a level number carried by an Enchantment - Class permanent, which enters at level 1 and is raised one step at a time by a printed "<cost>: Level N" ability that may be activated only as a sorcery and only when the permanent is at exactly level N-1 (levels cannot be skipped, and a level already gained cannot be bought again), plus a per-ability level gate so that each printed ability is active only at or above the level it is printed under, and every lower level's ability stays on. Concretely this wants (a) a level tracker on the permanent, (b) an ability form for the level line itself -- something like kind: "level" with level: 2 and a cost from cost_keys, the way kind: "chapter" carries chapter: 2 -- and (c) an optional level: N on any ability of any kind (triggered, static, activated) meaning "active only while this permanent is at level N or greater". With those three, Caretaker's Talent is: the token-draw trigger at level 1 (already expressible: permanent_enters, batched, filter {controller: "you", is_token: true}, max_per_turn: 1, effects draw 1), a level-2 line costing {"mana": "{W}"}, a level-2 triggered ability (see the trigger_event need below) whose effect is copy_permanent over a target token you control, a level-3 line costing {"mana": "{3}{W}"}, and a level: 3 static buff {"effect": "buff", "power": 2, "toughness": 2, "filter": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Creature"], "is_token": true}}. The effect bodies are all already sayable; only the level scaffolding is missing.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The nearest thing in reference is the Saga machinery -- ability_kinds has "chapter", ability_keys has "chapter", trigger_events has "chapter" -- and it is the wrong shape in every respect that matters. A Saga's chapters advance by themselves, one lore counter each precombat main phase, in a fixed order the player cannot pay to change; they fire once as a triggered ability and are then spent, and the Saga sacrifices itself at the end. Class levels are bought with mana at sorcery speed, only when the player chooses, and once bought they stay switched on for the rest of the game as a permanent characteristic-defining gate on OTHER abilities -- including a static one. A chapter cannot express "this static anthem is on from now on", because a chapter is a trigger, not a state. Nothing else in reference reaches it either: `ops` has no op that raises a level, `cost_keys` has no level cost, `ability_keys` has no level field, `static_condition_keys` has no level test, and `trigger_events` has no level event. The counter emulation is the dead end and was checked in full, so it does not need checking twice: an activated ability with sorcery_speed_only and cost {"mana": "{W}"} whose effect is add_counters of an invented "level" counter on itself, a static whose condition is a cmp on counters_on >= 2, and a counter_placed trigger filtered on that counter, does compile from the listed vocabulary but is not this card. It puts a counter on the permanent that the printed card does not describe as the thing being bought; it cannot enforce ascending order or one-purchase-per-level, because an ability's `condition` gates the ability's effect, not the legality of a repeat activation, so a player could buy level 2 four times and have four "level" counters; the counter_placed trigger fires again when the level-3 counter lands, so "When this Class becomes level 2" would create a second token copy at level 3; and every one of those abilities would have to claim a printed line it does not implement, which is exactly the half-implemented card the residual gate exists to catch. Per the brief, an approximation that quietly behaves differently is worse than nothing, so no partial answer was written.

needs.what: a "becomes level N" trigger event -- fires once, at the moment a Class permanent's level rises to exactly N, and never again (not when it later rises past N). It wants to be a trigger with source: "self" and a level: N key alongside `event`, the way `chapter` pairs with a chapter number, so that "When this Class becomes level 2, create a token that's a copy of target token you control" is a triggered ability whose effect is copy_permanent over a card-level target of kind permanent with selector {"controller": "you", "is_token": true}.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: trigger_events has 39 entries and none of them observe a level change. `chapter` is the closest and is Saga-only: it is driven by lore counters placed automatically at precombat main, not by a paid activation, so it cannot be pointed at a level purchase. `counter_placed` is the only event that fires off a permanent gaining something, and it is wrong twice over -- it would need the invented "level" counter from the engine need above to exist at all, and it fires on EVERY such counter, so the level-3 purchase would re-trigger the level-2 ability and make a second token copy. `ability_activated` fires when the level ability is activated rather than when the level is actually gained, which is a different moment (the level ability uses the stack, so the level-2 trigger must wait for it to resolve) and equally cannot tell level 2 from level 3.

notes: Only the level scaffolding is missing; every effect body on this card is already expressible and was deliberately not written as a partial answer. "Whenever one or more tokens you control enter, draw a card. This ability triggers only once each turn." is NOT blocked -- it is a triggered ability on permanent_enters with batched: true, filter {"controller": "you", "is_token": true} and max_per_turn: 1 (trigger_keys carries the printed rate limit, per the reference note) -- but it is the level-1 ability of a card whose remaining four printed lines cannot be said, so it does not rescue the card. Likewise "create a token that's a copy of target token you control" is copy_permanent over a target with selector {"controller": "you", "is_token": true}, and "Creature tokens you control get +2/+2" is a static buff whose filter uses is_token and types, both of which are in static_filter_keys. No token id is needed: the card copies an existing token rather than printing a new one, so this is not a `token` gap.
